chunks.title: 01 Rice Bacterial Leaf Blight
chunks.content:
# Bacterial Leaf Blight in Rice (Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae)

**Overview:**
Bacterial Leaf Blight (BLB) is one of the most destructive diseases affecting rice crops, particularly in warm, humid regions of Asia. It is caused by the bacterium *Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae*.

chunks.title: 01 Rice Bacterial Leaf Blight
chunks.content:
**Symptoms:**
- Water-soaked to yellowish lesions appear on leaf margins starting near the tips.
- Lesions expand along the leaf margins with characteristic wavy edges, turning light yellow to grayish-white.
- Bacterial ooze droplets (milky dew drops) may be observed on young infected leaves during early morning.
- In severe infections ("kresek" stage), whole leaves dry up, turn straw-colored, and die.

chunks.title: 01 Rice Bacterial Leaf Blight
chunks.content:
**Favorable Conditions:**
- High temperature (25–34°C), high relative humidity (>70%), heavy rain, and windy weather.
- Excessive application of nitrogenous fertilizers.

chunks.title: 01 Rice Bacterial Leaf Blight
chunks.content:
**Management & Decision Support Steps:**
1. Remove and destroy severely infected leaves or plants to prevent field spread.
2. Avoid excessive nitrogen application; split N doses appropriately.
3. Apply copper oxychloride (3 g/L) mixed with Streptocycline or copper hydroxide spray at early onset.
4. Ensure proper field drainage to eliminate standing stagnant water.

chunks.title: 02 Rice Blast
chunks.content:
# Rice Blast Disease (Magnaporthe oryzae)

**Overview:**
Rice blast is a major fungal disease caused by *Magnaporthe oryzae* (Pyricularia oryzae). It can infect leaves, leaf collars, nodes, panicles, and grain stems.

chunks.title: 02 Rice Blast
chunks.content:
**Symptoms:**
- Leaf blast: Spindle-shaped or diamond-shaped lesions with grayish-white centers and dark brown/reddish margins.
- Lesions enlarge and coalesce, causing entire leaf blades to wither and dry.
- Neck blast: Brown to blackish lesions at the panicle neck, causing panicles to fall over or remain unfilled ("whiteheads").

**Favorable Conditions:**
- Cool temperatures (20–25°C), high humidity (>90%), long dew periods, high soil nitrogen.

chunks.title: 02 Rice Blast
chunks.content:
**Management & Decision Support Steps:**
1. Avoid high nitrogen fertilization.
2. Apply systemic fungicides like Tricyclazole 75 WP (0.6 g/L) or Isoprothiolane 40 EC (1.5 mL/L) at first symptom appearance.
3. Maintain field moisture; avoid prolonged dry spells during vegetative stage.

chunks.title: 03 Rice Brown Planthopper
chunks.content:
# Brown Plant Hopper in Rice (Nilaparvata lugens)

**Overview:**
Brown Plant Hopper (BPH) is a sap-sucking insect pest of rice crops.

**Symptoms:**
- Insects cluster at the base of rice tillers near the water level.
- Infested leaves turn yellow-orange, then brown, dry up, and appear scorched ("hopperburn").
- Circular patches of dried plants appear in the field, expanding outward.
- Sooty mold growth develops on honeydew secreted by insects on lower stems.

chunks.title: 03 Rice Brown Planthopper
chunks.content:
**Management & Decision Support Steps:**
1. Drain irrigation water from the field for 3–4 days to disrupt pest multiplication.
2. Avoid excessive use of synthetic pyrethroids which kill natural predators.
3. Apply recommended insecticides like Triflumezopyrim 10 SC or Pymetrozine 50 WG targeting the base of plants.

chunks.title: 04 Wheat Yellow Rust
chunks.content:
# Wheat Yellow Rust / Stripe Rust (Puccinia striiformis f. sp. tritici)

**Overview:**
Yellow rust (stripe rust) is a devastating fungal disease of wheat crops in cooler agricultural zones.

**Symptoms:**
- Bright yellow to orange pustules arranged in linear stripes/stripes parallel to leaf veins.
- Pustules rupture leaf epidermis releasing yellow powdery urediniospores.
- Leaves dry prematurely, reducing grain filling and yield dramatically.

chunks.title: 04 Wheat Yellow Rust
chunks.content:
**Management & Decision Support Steps:**
1. Monitor field early during tillering and jointing stages.
2. Apply systemic triazole fungicide like Propiconazole 25 EC (1 mL/L) or Tebuconazole upon first detection of stripes.
3. Grow resistant wheat cultivars recommended by local agricultural extension.

chunks.title: 05 Wheat Powdery Mildew
chunks.content:
# Wheat Powdery Mildew (Blumeria graminis f. sp. tritici)

**Overview:**
Powdery mildew is a fungal disease affecting wheat leaves, sheaths, and ears in high-density foliage fields.

**Symptoms:**
- White to grayish fluffy talcum-like fungal patches on upper leaf surfaces.
- Patches enlarge, turn dull gray to light brown, with tiny black specks (cleistothecia).
- Affected leaves turn yellow, chlorotic, and die early.

chunks.title: 05 Wheat Powdery Mildew
chunks.content:
**Management & Decision Support Steps:**
1. Avoid dense seed sowing rates to promote canopy airflow.
2. Apply sulfur-based or hexaconazole fungicides if infection exceeds threshold level.

chunks.title: 06 Nitrogen Deficiency
chunks.content:
# Nitrogen Deficiency in Field Crops (Wheat, Rice, Maize)

**Overview:**
Nitrogen (N) is a mobile macro-nutrient essential for chlorophyll production and vegetative growth.

**Symptoms:**
- General yellowing (chlorosis) starting in older lower leaves from tip downward along midrib ("V-shaped" yellowing in maize).
- Stunted growth, thin stems, pale green young leaves.
- Premature senescense of lower foliage and poor tillering in cereals.

chunks.title: 06 Nitrogen Deficiency
chunks.content:
**Management & Decision Support Steps:**
1. Top-dress with Urea or ammonium nitrate dissolved in irrigation water.
2. Apply foliar spray of 1–2% Urea solution for rapid canopy absorption.
3. Test soil organic carbon and adjust basal N application rates.

chunks.title: 07 Phosphorus Deficiency
chunks.content:
# Phosphorus Deficiency in Maize and Wheat

**Overview:**
Phosphorus (P) deficiency severely inhibits root growth and early seedling establishment.

**Symptoms:**
- Dark green to reddish-purple pigmentation along leaf margins and stems (anthocyanin accumulation).
- Delayed maturity, weak root development, slender stalks.
- Stunted overall plant height.

chunks.title: 07 Phosphorus Deficiency
chunks.content:
**Management & Decision Support Steps:**
1. Apply soil phosphorus fertilizer (Single Super Phosphate / DAP) close to root zones during sowing.
2. Maintain soil pH between 6.0–7.5 for optimal phosphorus availability.

chunks.title: 08 Potassium Deficiency
chunks.content:
# Potassium Deficiency in Field Crops

**Overview:**
Potassium (K) regulates stomatal opening, water balance, and stress tolerance in plants.

**Symptoms:**
- Marginal leaf scorching or firing (browning along leaf edges) on older leaves.
- Leaves appear burnt at margins while central midrib area remains green.
- Increased susceptibility to lodging (stem breakage) and fungal pathogens.

chunks.title: 08 Potassium Deficiency
chunks.content:
**Management & Decision Support Steps:**
1. Apply Muriate of Potash (MOP / KCl) or Potassium Sulfate during land preparation or early dressing.
2. Apply foliar potassium nitrate (KNO3) 1% spray for quick recovery during vegetative phase.

chunks.title: 09 Maize Fall Armyworm
chunks.content:
# Maize Fall Armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda)

**Overview:**
Fall Armyworm (FAW) is a highly destructive pest attacking maize whorls and tassels.

**Symptoms:**
- Ragged holes and extensive defoliation on leaf whorls.
- Sawdust-like frass (insect excrement) accumulated inside the central whorl.
- Larvae with inverted Y-shaped mark on head capsule visible inside whorls.

chunks.title: 09 Maize Fall Armyworm
chunks.content:
**Management & Decision Support Steps:**
1. Handpick larvae or apply neem cake powder into whorls in early stages.
2. Apply Chlorantraniliprole 18.5 SC (0.4 mL/L) or Emamectin Benzoate 5 SG directly into plant whorls using hand sprayer.

chunks.title: 10 Sugarcane Red Rot
chunks.content:
# Sugarcane Red Rot (Colletotrichum falcatum)

**Overview:**
Red Rot is known as the "cancer of sugarcane", causing massive yield loss and sugar quality deterioration.

**Symptoms:**
- Third or fourth leaf shows yellowing, drying, and wilting.
- Splitting open affected stalk reveals longitudinal red discoloration interrupted by white transverse bands.
- Alcoholic or sour odor emitted from internal split stalk tissues.

chunks.title: 10 Sugarcane Red Rot
chunks.content:
**Management & Decision Support Steps:**
1. Uproot and burn diseased clumps immediately.
2. Treat setts with Carbendazim (0.1%) or hot water (52°C for 30 minutes) prior to planting.
3. Adopt 2–3 year crop rotation with non-host crops like paddy or legumes.

chunks.title: 11 Cotton Whitefly
chunks.content:
# Cotton Whitefly & Leaf Curl Virus (Bemisia tabaci)

**Overview:**
Whiteflies transmit Cotton Leaf Curl Virus (CLCuV) while sucking sap from undersides of leaves.

**Symptoms:**
- Upward or downward curling of leaf margins, vein thickening, and enations (leaf-like outgrowths) on undersides.
- Honeydew accumulation causing black sooty mold growth on cotton bolls and foliage.
- Stunted plant growth and severely reduced boll formation.

chunks.title: 11 Cotton Whitefly
chunks.content:
**Management & Decision Support Steps:**
1. Install yellow sticky traps (15–20/acre) to monitor and capture adult whiteflies.
2. Spray Afidopyropen 50 g/L DC or Diafenthiuron 50 WP targeting leaf undersides.
3. Remove weed hosts near cotton fields.

chunks.title: 12 Tomato Late Blight
chunks.content:
# Tomato Late Blight (Phytophthora infestans)

**Overview:**
Late blight is a fast-spreading oomycete disease in tomato crops under cool, humid weather.

**Symptoms:**
- Dark, water-soaked irregular spots on leaves, expanding rapidly into large dark brown necrotized areas.
- White fungal sporangial growth on underside of leaves in high moisture.
- Stalks turn dark brown/black; green and ripe fruit develop greasy brown firm rot.

chunks.title: 12 Tomato Late Blight
chunks.content:
**Management & Decision Support Steps:**
1. Apply contact fungicides like Mancozeb 75 WP (2.5 g/L) prophylactically before humid weather.
2. Apply systemic fungicides like Metalaxyl + Mancozeb (2 g/L) or Dimethomorph upon disease onset.
3. Avoid overhead sprinklers; ensure wide plant spacing for airflow.

chunks.title: 13 Tomato Early Blight
chunks.content:
# Tomato Early Blight (Alternaria solani)

**Overview:**
Early blight affects older lower leaves first and moves upward in warm temperatures with dew or rain.

**Symptoms:**
- Concentric ring lesions ("target spot" pattern) on lower leaves with dark brown borders.
- Leaves yellow around lesions, drop prematurely, exposing fruit to sunscald.
- Dark sunken lesions with concentric rings at stem ends of fruits.

chunks.title: 13 Tomato Early Blight
chunks.content:
**Management & Decision Support Steps:**
1. Mulch soil surface to prevent soil splash onto lower leaves.
2. Spray Chlorothalonil 75 WP (2 g/L) or Azoxystrobin (1 mL/L) at 7–10 day intervals.

chunks.title: 14 Potato Late Blight
chunks.content:
# Potato Late Blight (Phytophthora infestans)

**Overview:**
Potato late blight can wipe out entire potato fields within days if weather remains wet and temperatures are between 15–22°C.

**Symptoms:**
- Pale green to dark water-soaked leaf spots, turning brown to purplish-black.
- White mildew/mold growth visible on lower leaf surfaces during moist mornings.
- Tubers exhibit rusty-brown dry rot extending into flesh under skin.

chunks.title: 14 Potato Late Blight
chunks.content:
**Management & Decision Support Steps:**
1. Destroy volunteer potato plants and infected crop debris.
2. Spray Cymoxanil + Mancozeb (2 g/L) or Infinito (Fluopicolide + Propamocarb) immediately upon fog/humidity alert.
3. Perform proper earthing-up to cover tubers deeply with soil.

chunks.title: 15 Potato Soft Rot
chunks.content:
# Potato Blackleg and Soft Rot (Pectobacterium / Dickeya spp.)

**Overview:**
Bacterial soft rot and blackleg affect potato haulms and harvested tubers in warm, wet soils.

**Symptoms:**
- Inky black slimy rot at the base of stems (blackleg) originating from infected seed tubers.
- Stunted growth, yellowing upper leaves, wilting and collapse of main stems.
- Tubers turn soft, watery, and produce foul-smelling liquid breakdown.

chunks.title: 15 Potato Soft Rot
chunks.content:
**Management & Decision Support Steps:**
1. Use certified disease-free seed tubers; avoid cutting tubers before planting if soil is wet.
2. Plant in well-drained soils; avoid excessive over-irrigation.
3. Allow tuber skin to harden in dry soil before harvesting.

chunks.title: 16 Zinc Deficiency
chunks.content:
# Micronutrient Zinc Deficiency in Rice ("Khaira") and Wheat

**Overview:**
Zinc deficiency is extremely widespread in calcareous, alkaline, or continuously submerged paddy soils.

**Symptoms:**
- In rice ("Khaira" disease): 2–3 weeks after transplanting, younger leaves develop rusty-brown bronze spots that coalesce covering the leaf.
- In wheat and maize: White to light yellow bands on both sides of midrib on upper leaves ("white bud").
- Severe growth stunting and delayed crop maturity.

chunks.title: 16 Zinc Deficiency
chunks.content:
**Management & Decision Support Steps:**
1. Apply Zinc Sulfate heptahydrate (21% Zn @ 25 kg/ha) during basal soil preparation.
2. Spray 0.5% Zinc Sulfate + 0.25% Lime solution as a foliar application twice at 10-day intervals.

chunks.title: 17 Environmental Stress
chunks.content:
# Environmental Stress: Waterlogging & Heat/Drought Scorching

**Overview:**
Abiotic environmental factors such as prolonged water stagnation or extreme heat waves cause physiological damage mimicking disease.

**Symptoms:**
- Waterlogging: Yellowing and dropping of lower leaves, root decay (black, sour roots), wilted leaves despite abundant soil water.
- Heat/Drought stress: Tip burn, leaf rolling, floral drop, sunscald on fruits, brown crispy leaf margins.

chunks.title: 17 Environmental Stress
chunks.content:
**Management & Decision Support Steps:**
1. Dig surface field trenches to drain excess water within 24 hours of heavy rains.
2. Apply light frequent irrigation or micro-sprinklers during heat waves.
3. Apply foliar potassium nitrate (1%) or salicylic acid to enhance crop stress resilience.

chunks.title: 18 Ipm Guidelines
chunks.content:
# Integrated Pest & Disease Management (IPM) Protocols

**Overview:**
Integrated Pest Management combines biological, mechanical, cultural, and targeted chemical measures for sustainable crop protection.

chunks.title: 18 Ipm Guidelines
chunks.content:
**General Guidelines:**
1. Practice regular field scouting twice a week.
2. Maintain balanced fertilizer application based on soil test results (avoid N excess).
3. Encourage natural enemies (ladybird beetles, chrysoperla, parasitoid wasps) by avoiding broad-spectrum sprays during early crop stage.
4. When pest intensity exceeds Economic Threshold Level (ETL), use eco-friendly biopesticides (Neem oil 10,000 ppm, *Trichoderma viride*, *Bacillus thuringiensis*) before synthetic chemicals.
5. If confidence in diagnosis is low, consult local agricultural extension officers or Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) experts before mass chemical application.
